chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Ala' ibn Fudayl, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "The nature made by Allah is which He has made men."

key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: The Mighty and High (honorific for Allah)
key_terms.فِطْرَة: Natural disposition or innate nature created by God

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Fitrah in the Quran according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Tawhid*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interpreting the 'fitrah' of Surah Ar-Rum as 'Tawhid', establishing the innate human disposition toward monotheism as a foundational theological principle. This concise exegesis underscores that recognition of God's oneness is not merely acquired knowledge but an inherent, primordial state embedded in human nature, a concept central to Shia epistemology and creed.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sinan, on the authority of al-`Ala ibn Fudayl that I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) to interpret the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High:
The nature made by Allah is which He has made men.
